key_insight: A transfer principle converts continuous elliptic Carleman estimates into mesh-uniform discrete estimates without added stabilization, with radial-weight parameters satisfying s ≤ ch^(-4/5).
engineering_relevance: The framework supports rigorous stability analysis for finite-element and finite-difference inverse boundary problems used to infer spatially varying coefficients.
method: Construct a shifted continuous problem whose Galerkin solution matches the reconstructed discrete state.
Use weighted approximation to transfer continuous Carleman bounds to the discrete operator.
Apply the estimates to discrete Calderón recovery from independently prescribed, potentially disjoint boundary patches.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical verification for piecewise affine finite elements with consistent or lumped mass and Cartesian finite differences, yielding a single logarithmic data term plus an O(h^(1/2)) mesh remainder.
watch_item: The inverse stability result assumes dimension d ≥ 3, agreement of potentials near the boundary, and uniformly stable discrete Dirichlet problems.
paper_title: A Transfer Principle for Elliptic Carleman Estimates: Application to Discrete Calderón Stability
